issue: Items test convertible debt (ASU 2020-06 single-liability model), conversion at carrying amount (book value method) and the relative-fair-value allocation for bonds with detachable warrants, but no FAR lesson teaches any of these. Induced conversions (ASU 2024-04, testable on the 2026 exam) are not covered anywhere either.
evidence: The far-bonds lesson has no convertible, warrant or conversion content. grep -i 'convertible|detachable|warrant' over content/far/**/lesson.md finds convertibles only in far-eps (if-converted EPS); no lesson covers issuer accounting for convertibles or warrants. The only other items are far-debt-other far-dbt-14 (warrants) and far-dbt-19 (conversion), also untaught. grep -i 'induced conversion' over content/ returns nothing. Reference sheet Part 2: ASU 2024-04 is eligible from 1/1/2026. All three items are non-optional practice items.
source: ASC 470-20-25-2 (detachable warrants: relative fair value); ASC 470-20-25-12 and 470-20-40-4 as amended by ASU 2020-06 (convertible debt as a single liability; conversion at carrying amount, no gain or loss); ASC 470-20-40-13 to 40-16 and ASU 2024-04 (induced conversions); review/reference/far-standards.md Part 2
fix: Add a section to the far-bonds lesson (or far-debt-other, then move the items there) titled 'Debt with conversion features and warrants'. Cover: (1) ASU 2020-06 — convertible debt without a bifurcated derivative or substantial premium is one liability; (2) conversion — credit the carrying amount, including unamortized premium/discount/issuance costs, to common stock and APIC, with no gain or loss; (3) detachable warrants — allocate proceeds by relative fair value, with the warrant portion credited to APIC and any resulting discount amortized; nondetachable features are not separated; (4) induced conversion expense = FV of the extra consideration (ASU 2024-04). Add a worked example and one check item.

issue: Skill is labeled 'analysis', difficulty 3, but the item is pure recall of a single rule (the own-credit portion of an FVO liability's fair value change goes to OCI). It has no facts to analyze and no computation. That is two skill levels off, and it distorts the module's Blueprint skill mix.
evidence: The stem asks only where the instrument-specific credit-risk portion is recognized. The answer is a memorized rule (ASC 825-10-45-5). The AICPA defines Analysis as examining and studying interrelationships, not recalling a rule.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering & Understanding vs. Analysis); ASC 825-10-45-5
fix: Relabel skill 'remembering', difficulty 1 (or 2). Or rewrite as a numeric analysis item, e.g. give a total FV decrease of $40,000, of which $15,000 is from own credit. The candidate splits the gain between NI ($25,000) and OCI ($15,000) and states the effect on equity.

issue: Sequencing: two far-bonds practice items test content first taught in later modules. far-bond-23 (gain/loss on calling bonds) is taught in far-debt-other, the next module. far-bond-28 (FVO own-credit to OCI) is taught in far-fair-value (unit far-u10, Area III). A learner practicing far-bonds right after its lesson meets untaught rules.
evidence: far-bonds lesson has no extinguishment or fair value option content. far-debt-other lesson lines 84-104 teach extinguishment. far-fair-value lesson lines 110-115 teach the FVO and own-credit-to-OCI. Module order in content/sections/far.yaml: far-bonds precedes far-debt-other, and far-fair-value comes much later.
fix: Move far-bond-23 to far-debt-other and far-bond-28 to far-fair-value (change moduleId). Or add a one-paragraph preview of each rule to the far-bonds lesson.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are overstated by one level. Nine single-step computations are labeled analysis, difficulty 3, but are application, difficulty 2; far-bond-20 (pure recall) is labeled application. Identical computations carry different labels across items. Because of this, the module appears to meet the FAR analysis target (35-45%) when it doesn't.
evidence: Items 21-27 are each one operation, e.g. 21: 91,889 x 4%; 22: 91,889 + 676; 23: 102,000 - 98,000; 25: 108,111 x 8%; 26: 105,000 - 20,000; 27: 103,000 x 8/104. 17 is 104,100 - 713; 19 is two products using the given factors. Twins: 24 (analysis/3) is the same computation as 12 (application/2); 25 (analysis/3) mirrors 16 (application/2); 23 vs far-dbt-07 (application/2); 27 vs far-dbt-14 (application/3). 20 asks only where DIC amortization is reported. Current practice+exam mix: analysis 11/30 = 37%. After relabeling: about 1/30 (far-bond-10), with remembering at 7/30 = 23%, above the 5-15% band.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation (R&U 5-15, Application 45-55, Analysis 35-45)
fix: Relabel 17, 19 and 21-27 as application, difficulty 2, and 20 as remembering, difficulty 1. To restore analysis coverage, add genuinely multi-step items. Examples: a year-end accrual with non-calendar interest dates (expense plus amortization for a partial period); the effect on net income and liabilities of using straight-line instead of effective interest across two years; the effective rate after debt issuance costs; bonds issued between interest dates at a discount, with the issuer's entry.

issue: The issue prices contradict the stated 'annual interest' terms: each price is the 5-year semiannual price. No maturity is given, so a candidate who checks the price cannot reconcile it. The keys still follow mechanically from the given price.
evidence: Recomputed. 14: 1,000,000 x 0.67556 + 50,000 x 8.11090 = 1,081,109, which is 4%/10 periods, i.e. semiannual; the 5-year annual price is 1,079,854 and 10-year annual is 1,134,202. 25: 108,111 is the same semiannual price at 1/10 scale; 5-year annual is 107,985. x2-24: 1,000,000 x 0.7441 + 25,000 x 8.5302 = 957,355, i.e. 3%/10 periods semiannual; 5-year annual is 957,876.
fix: State a 5-year term and use annual-consistent prices, then recompute. 14: price 1,079,854; expense 86,388; carrying amount 1,066,242. 25: price 107,985; expense 8,639. x2-24: price 957,876; expense 57,473. Rebuild distractors from the new numbers. Alternatively, keep the prices, state 'semiannual', and recompute keys per period.

issue: Chained items depend on each other and leak answers. far-bond-02 ('Using the inputs in the previous item') restates far-bond-01's key (3.5% per period, 4% per period, 10 periods). far-bond-22 ('the bonds above') gives far-bond-21's key ($3,676). far-bond-17 ('previous facts') shows far-bond-16's key (7,287) in its feedback. Practice sessions are shuffled, so the 'previous' item is usually not previous, and the items can appear in either order or alone.
evidence: src/lib/quiz.ts lines 84-98 and 114-135 shuffle the eligible items (shuffle(...), interleave(...)), so item order is not preserved. Stem of 22: '(issued at $91,889, $3,676 expense, $3,000 cash)'. Stem of 02: '($200,000 face, 3.5% per period, 4% market per period, 10 periods)'.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing the answer to another)
fix: Make each item self-contained. Delete 'previous item/facts/above' wording. In 02, 17 and 22 give only the raw bond terms, so the candidate derives the intermediate amounts. Or merge each pair into a single two-step item (e.g. 22 asks for the carrying amount from the raw terms, which also tests 21).

issue: Answer cues. In far-bond-01 the key is the only option that says 'per period' (twice) and is much the longest. In far-bond-06 the key is the only compound statement (two true facts joined by a semicolon) and the longest option.
evidence: 01 key: '3.5% coupon per period, 4% market rate per period, 10 periods'; the other options name rates with no period qualifier. 06 key: 'Expense is below cash paid; carrying amount falls to face'; the other options are single clauses. cues.md flags both.
fix: 01: use a parallel format for every option, e.g. 'Coupon rate per period / market rate per period / number of periods: 7%/4%/10; 7%/8%/5; 3.5%/8%/10; 3.5%/4%/10'. 06: make each option a single clause of similar length, e.g. key 'Interest expense is less than the cash paid each period'.

issue: Trap labels don't match the misconception each distractor models. Recurring patterns: 'that's the cash interest' is labeled wrong-classification, and straight-line amounts are labeled wrong-classification or distractor-number. Several period errors are labeled distractor-number or wrong-rule.
evidence: 12c $106,000 = a full year's interest: wrong-rule, should be wrong-period. 14d and 18c (straight-line): wrong-classification, should be wrong-rule. 17c $103,280 = 104,100 - 4,100/5 (straight-line): distractor-number, should be wrong-rule. 16a, 21b, 25b, x2-24b (cash coupon): wrong-classification, should be partial-computation, as chk1(a) labels the same error. 16b $7,000 = 100,000 x 7% (yield x face): partial-computation, should be wrong-rule. 21c $7,351 = 91,889 x 8% (annual rate): distractor-number, should be wrong-period. 22a $91,213 = 91,889 - 676: wrong-rule, should be wrong-sign. 24b $103,000 (six months) and 24c $102,000 (4 months to the next coupon): distractor-number, should be wrong-period. 25d $1,351 is the amortization, not a reversal: reversed, should be partial-computation.
fix: Relabel the traps as listed in the evidence. Rewrite 17c's explanation as 'Straight-line amortization (4,100 / 5 = 820) — the effective interest method is required.' Rewrite 24c's as 'Accrues 4 months to the next coupon date; accrued interest runs from the last interest date (Jan 1) to the issue date (Mar 1).'

issue: Weak distractors and circular explanations. Several distractors model no misconception (trap 'distractor-number'), and their explanations say only 'Not the computation.' In far-bond-28, (b) is explained as 'Not the treatment.' and (c) as 'It is recognized.' These tell the learner nothing.
evidence: 16d $7,180, 22d $92,889 (91,889 + 1,000), 23d $6,000 loss, 25c $9,000 and 27d $3,000 (103,000 - 100,000) each carry the explanation 'Not the computation.' and no plausible error path.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ checks 2 and 4
fix: Replace each with a distractor built from a real error, and explain it. 16d: $8,328 = 104,100 x 8% (stated rate on carrying amount). 22d: $92,700 = 91,889 + 8,111/10 (straight-line). 23d: a $2,000 gain (face - carrying amount mistaken for a gain). 25c: $8,000 = face x yield. 27d: $95,077 = 103,000 x 96/104 (the bonds' share, not the warrants'). 28b/c: explain the actual rule — FVO changes are never charged directly to retained earnings, and FVO liabilities are remeasured every period, so changes are always recognized.

issue: Some distractor explanations don't reproduce their distractor's number, or need a fact the stem doesn't give.
evidence: x2-15(d) $945,000 is explained as 'Uses the stated rate on face value as the amortization', but the number is 925,000 + (8% x 1,000,000 - 60,000) = 945,000, i.e. the market rate applied to face. The stated-rate reading would give 985,000. x2-24(d) $54,256 is explained as a sign error ('Discount amortization increases, not decreases, expense'), but 50,000 - 7,441 = 42,559 and no sign error yields 54,256; it equals 60,000 - 5,744. 14(d) $1,073,000 'uses straight-line', which requires a 10-year term (81,109/10 = 8,111), but no term is stated. 26(a) $80,000 implies a $100,000 face that the stem never gives.
fix: x2-15(d): explanation 'Applies the 8% market rate to face value (80,000) instead of the carrying amount.' x2-24(d): change the number to 42,559 (cash - amortization) to match the explanation, or rewrite the explanation. 14: state the term (and fix the price per the inconsistent-price finding) so that (d) is derivable. 26: state the face ($100,000), or replace (a) with a computable error (e.g. $105,000 - $20,000 par - $5,000 premium = $80,000, with that explained).

issue: The key's wording '(net of a $5,000 discount)' misdescribes the presentation. There is no discount: a $10,000 premium and $15,000 of unamortized debt issuance costs are separate components that net to $995,000. This blurs the ASU 2015-03 presentation the item is testing.
evidence: Proceeds at 101 = 1,010,000, a premium of 10,000. Issuance costs of 15,000 are a direct deduction. Net carrying amount = 1,000,000 + 10,000 - 15,000 = 995,000. The item's own explanation describes it correctly ('premium 10,000 less issuance costs 15,000').
fix: Reword the key: 'Net carrying amount of $995,000 (face $1,000,000 plus $10,000 premium less $15,000 unamortized debt issuance costs)'. Keep the other options parallel in length.

issue: far-bond-12 and far-bond-24 are near-duplicates: $100,000 of 6% bonds issued at par on March 1, two months of accrued interest, key $101,000 in both. The only difference is the coupon dates, which don't change the computation. Together with lesson check far-bond-chk2 and the lesson's worked example, the same fact is tested the same way four times.
evidence: 12: '$100,000 of 6% bonds at par, dated January 1, interest annually December 31, issued March 1' gives 101,000. 24: '$100,000 of 6% bonds paying interest January 1 and July 1, issued at par on March 1' gives 101,000. chk2: April 1, $400,000 at 9%, 3 months, 409,000.
fix: Replace far-bond-24 with a different between-dates task. Options: the issuer's journal entry on issuance (Cr Interest payable 1,000), net interest expense for the first period (18,000 coupon - 6,000 accrued = 12,000), or issuance between dates at a discount.

issue: One-step effective-interest drills are over-represented in practice, and multi-step scenarios are missing. First-period interest expense (carrying amount x market rate) is tested 4 times: 16, 18, 21, 25. Carrying amount after one payment is tested 4 times: 04, 14, 17, 22. Both are also in the exam pool (x2-15, x2-24) and both TBS. No practice item covers a year-end accrual with amortization when interest dates don't match the year-end, multi-period schedules, the effective rate after issuance costs, or the issuance journal entry.
evidence: Counts from items.json: expense drills 16/18/21/25 (+ chk1, x2-24, TBS i1); carrying-amount drills 04/14/17/22 (+ x2-15, TBS c1/cv1). Each is a single multiply or add.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than 3 times)
fix: Convert two of each cluster into higher-order items, e.g. (a) bonds dated Apr 1 with Apr 1/Oct 1 coupons and a Dec 31 year-end: accrued interest plus partial-period discount amortization at Dec 31; (b) interest expense for Year 2, requiring a two-period schedule; (c) DIC: net proceeds and the resulting interest expense; (d) the issuance JE with discount.

issue: Lesson gaps on commonly tested mechanics. It never shows the issuance journal entry (Dr Cash, Dr Discount, Cr Bonds payable), year-end accrual of interest plus partial-period amortization when interest dates differ from the fiscal year-end, zero-coupon bonds (tested by far-bond-18), or the effect of debt issuance costs on the effective rate. Its only issuance-cost content is one presentation sentence.
evidence: The lesson body (lines 40-121) contains only the June 30 interest JE. The between-dates example has no amortization. No year-end adjusting entry and no zero-coupon example. far-bond-09 (accrual) and far-bond-18 (zero-coupon) are derivable but not taught.
fix: Add (1) the issuance JE for the worked example (Dr Cash 875,378; Dr Discount 124,622; Cr Bonds payable 1,000,000); (2) a short faded example of a Dec 31 adjusting entry for bonds with Apr 1/Oct 1 coupons, with accrued interest and 3 months of amortization; (3) one sentence that a zero-coupon bond's entire return is discount accretion; (4) a DIC example showing net proceeds and the higher effective rate.

issue: Lesson metadata. The third objective (debt issuance costs and between-dates issuance) has no Blueprint 'task' mapping, while the other two do. The citations name the broad topics (ASC 470-10, 835-30) rather than the paragraphs the lesson relies on.
